description: First native-system import pass covering character creation, attributes, derived statistics, origins, careers, skills, motivations, ancestry options, cyborg variants, the full-cyberization threshold, and pre-cyberization data seizures. Source ambiguities are recorded rather than replaced with another RPG system.

entries.title: Character Creation System
entries.summary: Solanum Umbra characters are built through six 1d20 attributes, four derived statistics, an origin, a career path, career benefits and skills, a personal motivation, ancestry choices, and optional cyberization.
body: The source presents character creation as a sequence of direct rolls and selections rather than a point-buy or borrowed class framework. Each of the six attributes is rolled on 1d20 and used at its rolled value.

The character then records four derived statistics: Health, Armor, Initiative, and SKILL. Origin, career, career benefits, career skills, and personal motivation establish the character’s practical identity in the post-collapse world.

Advanced creation allows Pre-Fall Human, Post-Fall Human, Fae, and cyberized variants. Characters exceeding 49% cybernetic replacement must undergo full cyberization or begin accumulating escalating data seizures and systemic errors.
This wiki preserves the native Solanum Umbra procedures. It does not convert the system into Hypertext d20, 3.5, or another rules chassis.
creationSequence: Roll 1d20 for Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.
Roll or choose an origin from the source origin table.
Determine a career path and its benefits.
Roll or choose a personal history or motivation.
Apply final adjustments arising from career and history.
For advanced creation, select ancestry and any cyborg variant.
Record cybernetic body percentage and full-cyberization status when applicable.

sourceRefs.notes: Character creation, attributes, derived statistics, origins, careers, skills, motivations, ancestry comparisons, cyborg variants, full-cyberization requirement, and data-seizure progression.

entries.title: Core Attributes and Derived Statistics
entries.summary: Six attributes are rolled on 1d20 and combined into Health, Armor, Initiative, and SKILL using the native Solanum Umbra formulas.
body: Strength measures physical power and endurance. Dexterity measures agility, reflexes, and precision. Constitution measures health, stamina, and resilience. Intelligence measures knowledge and problem solving. Wisdom measures perception, intuition, and common sense. Charisma measures persuasion and leadership.

The source uses the rolled attribute value directly. It also supplies a broad bonus and penalty table. The 9–11 range is printed as ‘-1 to +1’ rather than assigning one exact value to each score; this remains marked as a source ambiguity pending a later native-system editorial ruling.

entries.title: Origins, Careers, Skills, and Motivations
entries.summary: A character’s place in the wasteland is established by an origin, a career path, career-specific benefits and skills, and a personal motivation.
body: The origin and motivation tables have explicit 1d20 ranges. The source lists six career paths but gives only one example roll producing a Mechanic and does not publish a complete career roll-range table. The wiki therefore preserves the career list and marks the missing mapping as unresolved instead of inventing one.

Career benefits and additional skills are intended to use career-specific 1d20 tables. Pages 106–107 provide the Mechanic as the complete example. Other careers will be indexed from later source sections before any missing benefit table is authored.

entries.title: Ancestries and Cyborg Variants
entries.summary: Advanced character creation distinguishes Pre-Fall Humans, Post-Fall Humans, Fae, and cyberized variants of each ancestry through qualitative attribute tendencies.
body: The source describes ancestry tendencies qualitatively rather than assigning a complete numerical modifier package in pages 109–112. The wiki preserves those descriptions as guidance and does not invent bonuses.

Pre-Fall Humans are balanced baselines. Post-Fall Humans are adaptive survivors emphasizing Dexterity, Wisdom, social alliance-building, and environmental resilience. Fae emphasize Dexterity, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma but possess lower physical resilience. Cyborg variants combine ancestry with cybernetic reinforcement and processing.

entries.title: The 49% Full-Cyberization Threshold
entries.summary: A character replacing more than 49% of the body with cybernetics must complete full cyberization or suffer escalating interface conflicts, data seizures, and systemic decline.
body: The threshold is explicit: more than 49% cybernetic replacement requires comprehensive integration into a cohesive system. The process aligns interfaces, updates control architecture, calibrates components, and reduces conflict between disparate implants.
Postponement causes glitches, loss of control, disrupted sensory input, malfunctioning limbs, failed interfaces, cognitive decline, and eventually catastrophic system failure or death.

The rule is also a character-development engine. Securing full cyberization may require specialized technicians, protected facilities, rare power systems, calibration software, and difficult choices about identity and dependence.

sourceRefs.notes: 49% threshold, data seizures, integration purpose and outcome, consequences of postponement, and roleplaying considerations.

entries.title: Pre-Cyberization Data Seizures and Errors
entries.summary: Six escalating stages track the consequences of remaining above 49% replacement without full cyberization, from minor glitches during the first week to fatal system collapse after eighteen months.
body: The source combines skill penalties, percentage performance loss, increased error rates, and action-failure chances. These values are recorded as separate native-system consequences and should not be translated into another game’s conditions.

The table’s wording occasionally overlaps percentage error rate and action failure. The wiki preserves both because the manuscript treats them as distinct measurements, even where the precise resolution sequence will require later native-system editing.

tables.title: Data-seizure progression
rows: Intermittent glitches, reduced sensory precision, mild disorientation
Disrupted actions, reduced precision, slower reactions
Persistent malfunctions, major agility and control loss, frequent seizures
Severe data corruption, loss of control, system crashes, inability to perform complex tasks
Constant instability, full seizures, cognitive and motor loss, severe implant malfunction
Total system failure, uncontrollable seizures, complete functional loss, imminent death

sourceRefs.notes: Six-stage native progression of errors, skill penalties, performance loss, error rates, action failure, and final collapse.

entries.title: Native Character Sheet Fields
entries.summary: A structured field map for recording the native character-creation information already defined in the source, without adding foreign statistics.
body: This field map is a wiki and future-tool schema, not a replacement rules system. It records only elements present in or directly required by the native character-creation text.
Later passes will append equipment, cybernetic replacement details, biotic power requirements, combat values, progression, role features, and crafting records from their own source sections.

sourceRefs.notes: Sheet field structure derived strictly from native character-creation and cyberization records.
